title: E-Commerce Schema Design
description: Design a normalized schema for an e-commerce platform with products, orders, and inventory

data.text: E-commerce platforms need schemas that handle products, categories, customers, carts, orders, payments, and shipments. A good design prevents anomalies and supports common queries without excessive joins.

data.title: Key entities
items: Order: header with totals and status

data.title: E-commerce DDL
data.content: Create core tables with proper keys and foreign keys.
data.code:
CREATE TABLE products (
  product_id INT PRIMARY KEY AUTO_INCREMENT,
  sku VARCHAR(64) UNIQUE NOT NULL,
  name VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
  price DECIMAL(10,2) NOT NULL,
  stock INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  category_id INT,
  created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
);

CREATE TABLE categories (
  category_id INT PRIMARY KEY AUTO_INCREMENT,
  name VARCHAR(120) NOT NULL,
  parent_category_id INT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE orders (
  order_id INT PRIMARY KEY AUTO_INCREMENT,
  customer_id INT NOT NULL,
  total DECIMAL(10,2) NOT NULL,
  status VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL,
  created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
);

CREATE TABLE order_items (
  order_item_id INT PRIMARY KEY AUTO_INCREMENT,
  order_id INT NOT NULL,
  product_id INT NOT NULL,
  quantity INT NOT NULL,
  unit_price DECIMAL(10,2) NOT NULL
);

data.title: Tip
data.text: Store unit_price in order_items, not products, so historical orders keep their original price even if product prices change later.

items.question: Should categories support unlimited nesting?
items.answer: Use an adjacency list with parent_category_id for most cases. For deep hierarchies, consider a closure table or nested set.

items.question: How do I prevent overselling?
items.answer: Use row-level locking or atomic UPDATE with CHECK constraints. Avoid storing denormalized stock counts outside inventory tables.

items.question: Do I need a separate addresses table?
items.answer: Yes. Customers and orders often need both billing and shipping addresses. Reusing addresses avoids duplication and supports historical accuracy.

data.title: Summary
points: Capture price at order time in order_items
Separate addresses from customers and orders
data.takeaway: A good e-commerce schema isolates mutable data and preserves historical accuracy for financial and operational queries.
